root_cause.text: The i.MX8MP HDMI block controller driver incorrectly gated the NOC_HDCP clock in the HDCP power-domain path, allowing the NoC ADB400 port power-down handshake to stall and hang the system.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes per-domain clock disable/enable handling for `IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP` in `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on()`/`power_off()` and changes `imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier()` to always set `BIT(11)` in `HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0`, matching the commit message “Keep the NOC_HDCP clock always enabled to fix the potential hang caused by the NoC ADB400 port power down handshake.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the HDCP power-on clock bit programming from the HDMI block controller sequence.
intent_record.what: The switch case for `IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP` was removed from `imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_on()`, so the function no longer sets `BIT(11)` in `HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0` when powering on that power-domain state.
intent_record.how: At runtime, requests to power on the HDCP-related block will no longer perform that clock-bit enable operation. This changes the hardware bring-up sequence for the HDCP domain and prevents that specific register write from occurring during power-on.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the HDCP-specific clock bit clear from HDMI block power-off handling.
intent_record.what: The switch case for IMX8MP_HDMIBLK_PD_HDCP was removed from imx8mp_hdmi_blk_ctrl_power_off(), deleting the regmap_clear_bits() call that cleared BIT(11) in HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 during power-off.
intent_record.how: HDCP power-off no longer performs a dedicated clock-bit clear in this function, so that bit is left unchanged here instead of being explicitly disabled when the HDCP block is powered down.

intent_record.intent_summary: Enable an additional HDMI RTX clock control bit during power sequencing to fix hardware initialization or operation.
intent_record.what: In imx8mp_hdmi_power_notifier(), the regmap_set_bits() call for HDMI_RTX_CLK_CTL0 was changed to set BIT(11) in addition to the existing BIT(0), BIT(1), and BIT(10) flags.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the HDMI RTX clock control register is programmed with one additional bit enabled during the power notification path, which likely activates an extra required clock or related hardware function for correct HDMI operation.
